top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B010) credits one identifiable discovery: firm heterogeneity and selection in trade theory. It yields predictions that representative-firm trade models do not produce (exporter premia, selection into exporting and foreign investment, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) and that firm-level data have tested for over twenty years. The credit line follows the intellectual structure, with Melitz (2003) as the model and Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple extending it to exporting versus foreign investment. The remaining costs are precursor credit (Bernard, Jensen, Eaton, Kortum, Hopenhayn) and Redding's omission. Both can be handled through a narrow citation on selection and reallocation and through the scientific background. The citation should not rest on welfare magnitudes, which depend on distributional assumptions. This is my assessment on the evidence, not on the size of the supporting group. It is the only awarding proposal on the slate, and I rank it above no award because the contribution is mature, significant and attributable.
